ratings_why.fun: Over a 7 because Hendrika's twice-a-turn budget is a real sequencing puzzle every turn: spend it on Sluice Keeper, the Millwright or Aaltje's fight Raise, while Millwright's order at the caps and the Dike/Afloat slots add more choices.
ratings_why.distinct: Over a 7 because one visible Level that floods both front rows, yours included, plays like no current tribe: you build your front row around the water instead of around attacks.

verdict_why: The rules now read cleanly and the engines are bounded; more passes would change the flavour of the combos, not improve them.

points.text: Hendrika and Aaltje share one turn budget, so carrying the fight Raise to 5 for free permanent payoffs competes with recruit-phase carries. Show the remaining charges on the card in the fight, because this is the tribe's best decision.

Bench Coot is the plainest card, but with Objecting Coot every buy-and-sell of it is two or three Raises. A small "when sold, if the Level is 5, gain 1 gold" would make that sell loop a deliberate line, not a side effect.
Ring-Dike pays only on Raises, so in the Minutes build Millwright makes it pay every turn. Keep the split: it makes picking between Ring-Dike and Ditch-Digger a real choice.
Tail-Slapper with a cheap 1-Health unit standing in your own Flood is a self-made trigger, and with Kees each re-Flood also stacks Attack. Worth naming that line in High Water so players find it.
Winter Raft wants the turn to end at 0 while High Water wants 5, so with Aaltje it is the one card that rewards draining hard and flooding anyway. A line in the Dry Polder build saying so would help.

standouts.why: Hendrika turns every single vote into a full swing, and her twice-a-turn limit shared with the fight makes her a puzzle, not a button.
Polder Millwright makes two changes without moving the Level, and its order matters at 0 and 5: a small card that holds the swing build together.
Tail-Slapper makes your own deaths a resource, links to Kees and Oozes, and its cap stops the cascade.

weakest.why: Bench Coot does one obvious job; its only interest comes from Objecting Coot.
Aaltje is a flat Start of Combat Raise; her depth comes entirely from Hendrika and the Raise payoffs.
Inspecting Heemraad is a placement-locked buffer that reads the Level but makes no decision of its own.

flags.note: Hendrika with Kobus Bles and Master of the Nine Mills: one carried Drain from 5 gives about +14/+14 to every unit, and twice a turn. Bounded, but the high roll to sim.
Aaltje's fight Raise carried by Hendrika gives permanent payoffs every fight, then resets for free, so the Level costs nothing to swing again.
Kobus Bles doubles Hendrika too, since she triggers on Raise or Drain; say whether the doubled copy can carry, or that it does nothing once at 5 or 0.
